note: Changes that are finished but are waiting for the next card update, because sending one costs a signed update to every card in a customer's home. Run "npm run firmware:waiting" to read this, and "npm run firmware:release" to carry it all at once.

waiting.what: Preserve section differences when adjusting a complete look and restore its saved default on startup.
waiting.why: Not yet proven on a card. The refusals seen on the 1.2.5 candidate 4e254c3b (23 Nov 2026) were not caused by this change: they were the older client-pattern save fault (a save straight after a query GET is refused), which my direct test triggered and which is in signed 1.2.4 too. It needs a re-check through Studio's real save path (POST /api/config) and the phone player before it is sent.
stillNeeds: Build the patched firmware and flash it to the real card over USB (bash scripts/firmware-dev.sh); confirm /api/firmware-info reports buildId dev.

Save a project that has per-section looks from Studio's real save path (the Save to card button, which sends POST /api/config); confirm the card accepts it with no 'invalid pattern envelope' or other refusal.
Read the looks back (/api/status and Studio's read-back) and confirm the sections differ the way they were saved.
On the phone player, nudge a complete look's brightness or speed and confirm the section differences are kept, not flattened.
Power-cycle the card and confirm it boots into the saved default look, not the first look.

Only after all five pass, drain with npm run firmware:release. The patch no longer applies cleanly with git apply (main moved); the release applies it with --3way, so run npm run firmware:waiting first and expect it to report if it truly conflicts.

waiting.what: Let a look save through the phone player go through when it comes straight after reading that look's settings.
waiting.why: On every card since 1.2.4, a look save sent right after a GET /api/client-pattern?patternId=… is refused with "invalid pattern envelope": the GET's query argument is still counted when the save is checked. No owner path reaches it today: Studio saves looks through /api/config, and the phone player reads the card status before each save, which clears it. One line in handleClientPatternPost plus a host test; it rides the next card release.

waiting.what: Add the crash-record format and its host tests: the pure code that turns a watchdog or panic reset into a saved record the card reports on /api/status.
waiting.why: Groundwork only: nothing in the firmware calls it yet, so it changes no card. The wiring (a breadcrumb in RTC memory, one NVS write per crash, the lastCrash field) is the next step in todo/plans/crash-recorder.md and needs a bench card, so this rides that card release.
